title: You were never meant to live this far from the Tree.
paragraphs: You were never meant to live this far from the Tree.

But you did.
And deep down… you know it.

You scroll.
You smile.
You perform.
But something inside you feels… off.
Like you lost something you can’t name.
Like you’re alive—but not fully alive.
And here’s the tension you can’t escape:
What if the emptiness you feel… is ancient?

What if it didn’t start with your last mistake—
but with the first one?
To a garden where everything was right.

No shame.
No hiding.
No pretending.
And right there—within reach—stood a tree.

“The Lord God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground—trees that were pleasing to the eye and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.” — Genesis 2:9

You hide behind success.
Behind humor.
Behind filtered versions of yourself.
And here’s the part most people miss:
He blocked access to the Tree of Life.
“After he drove the man out, he placed on the east side of the Garden of Eden cherubim and a flaming sword… to guard the way to the tree of life.” — Genesis 3:24

Because living forever in a broken state
would be a curse, not a gift.
But now you’re left with this ache.
Because your soul remembers something your mind forgot:
You were made for that Tree.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because the problem isn’t just what you’ve done.

You don’t need God—
until everything falls apart.
Some of us don’t run from God.
But it’s just distance dressed up nicely.
And the longer you live like that…
Until one day, you wake up and realize:

Not conviction.
Not hunger for God.
Not even guilt.
But God didn’t leave the story there.
He didn’t abandon humanity outside the garden.
He wrote Himself back into the narrative.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
The very thing that once represented lost life…
became the place where life was restored.
He took the punishment we deserved.
He absorbed the wrath meant for us.
He walked out of the grave.
Because in the final pages of Scripture—

“Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life… flowing from the throne of God… On each side of the river stood the tree of life… And the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.” — Revelation 22:1–2
“Blessed are those who wash their robes, that they may have the right to the tree of life…” — Revelation 22:14
Some scholars interpret the Tree of Life in Revelation as both a literal tree and a symbolic picture of eternal life in God’s presence.
What was lost… is offered again.
But you don’t walk back into Eden on your own terms.
You don’t earn your way there.
You don’t perform your way into life.
Leaving behind the life that’s killing you slowly.
Because you’re no longer cut off from the Tree.
“I am the way and the truth and the life.” — John 14:6
What are you going to do with this?
Keep feeding a soul that’s starving?
you won’t just read about the Tree of Life.
But don’t wait for that day to choose.
You might be the bridge God uses to bring them back.
And if something in you is waking up…
